solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Abrasive tool limits unsightly smirch in sailor’s hobby

indicators.note: something unsightly is messed up and out of shape, so the letters are put into disorder
to limit something is to bound it on both sides, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a power tool that smooths with abrasive paper
the letters of smirch, rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor's pastime of polishing carvings is spoilt by an ugly smudge from a sanding tool.
explanation.walkthrough: SANDER wraps round the jumbled SMIRCH to give SCRIMSHANDER, Chambers' variant of scrimshaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrimshaw, the carving of bone and ivory to pass time on long voyages, is the classic seaman's craft; scrimshander is an old name for it.

clue.text: Spruce twinkling brightness in the States revealing massed galaxies

indicators.note: twinkling suggests restless flickering movement, so the letters shift about

blocks.note: the letters of spruce, rearranged
the American spelling of lustre, a sheen or brightness

explanation.surface: An American stargazer sees a fir tree's glittering light and thinks of distant galaxies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' reads as a tree or an adjective for smart; it is just the letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercluster is a vast grouping of galaxy clusters, the largest known structures in the universe.

clue.text: Sweet treat on marble? Skater may perform this

blocks.note: short for a chocolate
a taw is a large marble used for shooting in the game

explanation.surface: A child munches a chocolate while playing marbles, then a skater appears.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across-or-down charade 'on' means placed after: the sweet comes first, then the marble.
explanation.definitionFit: A choctaw is a figure-skating step in which the skater changes foot and edge, moving from forward to backward.

clue.text: Essayist’s harsh attack about capital

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the attack word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: a raid is a sudden attack
capital letters are upper case, abbreviated u.c. by printers

explanation.surface: A writer describes a brutal assault on a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city to attack; it is the printer's term upper case, UC. The essayist is Charles Lamb, who used raucid in his Essays of Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucid is Lamb's coinage meaning hoarse or grating, a variant of raucous used in his essays.

clue.text: Old animal’s bolthole, opening for escape in frenzy

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start is kept
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: must is the frenzied state of a male elephant in rut
first letter of escape

explanation.surface: A hunted creature dashes for its hiding place in a panic, desperate to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: Must, as in an elephant 'on must', is a frenzy; the surface frenzy is the animal's panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A muset, or musit, is an archaic word for a gap in a hedge through which a hare or other animal escapes.

clue.text: Muslim of glorious memory has endless bubbliness

indicators.note: without an end means each word loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
fizz is effervescence

explanation.surface: A revered Muslim, fondly remembered, was full of fizzing high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims both words: HAS loses S and FIZZ loses a Z, giving HAFIZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A hafiz is a Muslim who has memorised the whole Koran, so his memory is literally a glorious one.

clue.text: Irani bowling introduces lifted trajectory – it’s intended to disconcert opponent

indicators.note: bowling suggests tumbling over and over, so the letters roll into a new order
in a down clue lifting a word turns it upside down, so it reads from the bottom
to introduce is to bring inside, so one piece is set within the other

blocks.note: the letters of Irani, rearranged
aim is the line or direction of a shot

explanation.surface: An Iranian bowler sends down a lofted delivery designed to unsettle the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture is pure misdirection; the answer is from sumo wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: Niramiai is the sumo ritual of glaring at the rival before a bout, a psychological tactic to unnerve him.

clue.text: Shrines for holy ones, erected like Gaudí’s masterpiece mostly?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
in a down clue erecting a word stands it up, so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: Gaudí's great Barcelona basilica is the Sagrada Família

explanation.surface: Holy shrines are built like Gaudí's unfinished Barcelona church, still mostly going up.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGRADA loses its last letter, then reads upward: DARGAS. The joke 'mostly' suits a church still under construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A dargah is the shrine or tomb of a Muslim saint; darga is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Blushing about love’s silly, showing firm determination

indicators.note: silly means foolish and muddled, so the letters are jumbled
about means going round, so the blushing word encloses the other

blocks.note: redness of the face when blushing
the letters of loves, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone blushes over a foolish romance yet stays stubbornly set on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolvedness is the quality of being resolved, that is fixed in purpose and decided.

clue.text: Clan group turned up behind Scots manor?

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the little word faces the other way

blocks.note: ha' is the Scots form of hall, a manor house
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clan gathering arrives at a Scottish laird's house, approaching from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' puts the reversed word after the Scots hall. The Scottish clan picture misleads: the answer is Maori.
explanation.definitionFit: A hapu is a Maori subtribe, a kinship division within an iwi or tribe.

clue.text: Stuff I had for meal following part of weekend in short

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the I-and-meal pieces are placed after the weekday piece

blocks.note: the short form of Saturday
taken as written
to have food for a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a big Saturday meal that left them stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT is the standard short form of Saturday, half of the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff someone is to fill them to repletion, which is to satiate them.

clue.text: Source of oil is shortly found in pork lard

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the short piece sits within the lard word

blocks.note: seame is an obsolete spelling of seam, meaning lard or grease
's is the contracted form of is

explanation.surface: A cook notes that some oil is quickly found in pork fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Seam (old spelling seame) is a dialect word for fat or lard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds are pressed to give sesame oil, widely used in cooking.

clue.text: Small monkey, one dashed off by Venetian master

indicators.note: dashed off means rushed away, so a piece departs from the painter's name

blocks.note: an means one
Titian was the great painter of the Venetian school

explanation.surface: A Venetian old master quickly sketches a tiny monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed off' looks like rapid painting; it means AN leaves TITIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The titi is a small South American monkey with long soft fur.

clue.text: Old-style lentils etc in soupes à l’étrangère?

indicators.note: French for in the foreign manner, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: the letters of soupes, rearranged

explanation.surface: Lentils and similar old-fashioned fare go into foreign-style soups.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase is the signal: soups done the foreign way have their letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pousse is Spenser's form of pulse, the edible seeds of legumes such as lentils, peas and beans.

clue.text: Wheel man in fathoms lapses circling island

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the lapses word encloses the island letter

blocks.note: F is an abbreviation for fathom
to err is to lapse or slip
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A helmsman with the depths in fathoms makes mistakes while steering round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheel man' suggests a helmsman; it is the inventor of a fairground wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: George Ferris built the first big observation wheel in 1893, and the Ferris wheel bears his name.

clue.text: Popular gathering cooked cecils in middle of meal

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are reworked
the middle of a word is its central letters only
in places the jumbled name inside the central letters

blocks.note: the two central letters of meal
the letters of cecils, rearranged

explanation.surface: A crowd assembles while some Cecils are cooked up halfway through dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cecils' looks like people's names; they are just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecclesia was the popular assembly of citizens in ancient Athens; the word later came to mean a church congregation.

clue.text: Beauty husband cut, a composite – great mishap

indicators.note: cut means removed, so that letter is taken out of the beauty word

blocks.note: a dish is an attractive person
H is the abbreviation for husband
the aster is a member of the daisy family, Compositae

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman's husband was dropped for some composite figure, a great calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: In botany a composite is a plant of the daisy family, Compositae; 'Beauty' as a dish is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden calamity, a misfortune on a large scale.

clue.text: Communication I kept in crock returned?

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the letter sits within the crock word
returned means sent back, so the whole reads in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a crock is a broken-down, disabled person, one who is lame
taken as written

explanation.surface: A message is stuffed into an earthenware pot and sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crock' suggests a pot; here it is a decrepit person, giving LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Email is electronic mail, a message sent between computers.

clue.text: Messenger from Scotland formerly that is trailing old errand boy

blocks.note: a cad was once an errand boy or assistant
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Scottish messenger of old trails behind a former errand boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cad originally meant an errand boy or omnibus conductor's helper before it came to mean a bounder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadie is an old Scots spelling of caddie, which once meant a street messenger or porter in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Clubs provided with money for repetition of parts

blocks.note: a meri is a Maori war club
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Clubs given funding to keep repeating the same spare parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' looks like the card suit or societies; they are Maori weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology merism is the repetition of similar parts, such as segments, in an organism's body.

clue.text: Short blades and so on alternating with call for help

indicators.note: alternating means taking turns, so the two pieces interleave letter by letter

blocks.note: etc. abbreviates et cetera
the distress signal

explanation.surface: Someone lists short blades and more, punctuated by cries for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters interleave one at a time, beginning with E of ETC: E, S, T, O, C, S.
explanation.definitionFit: An estoc was a short thrusting sword of the late Middle Ages.

clue.text: RC decoration encountered around part of Yorkshire?

indicators.note: around means going about, so the meeting word encloses the Yorkshire piece

blocks.note: to encounter is to meet
the Yorkshire Dales are a range of valleys in northern England

explanation.surface: A Roman Catholic award is found somewhere in the Yorkshire countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'RC decoration' sounds like church ornament; it is a small devotional medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A medalet is a small medal, especially one bearing a saint's image worn by Roman Catholics.

clue.text: Desires getting female in a state briefly

indicators.note: in places the female inside the short state name

blocks.note: Wis. is the abbreviation for Wisconsin
she is a female

explanation.surface: Someone's longings are met when a woman arrives in a US state for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishes and desires are both longings for something, nouns that are synonyms.

clue.text: Occupant of part of Asia Minor close to island in it

definitions.text: Occupant of part of Asia Minor

indicators.note: in places the combined piece inside the little word it

blocks.note: taken as written
on can mean next to, as a town on a river
Is. is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An Anatolian resident lives near an island in the region.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ionist is a native of Ionia, the Greek-settled coast of western Asia Minor.

clue.text: What’s enfolding shrimati, see? I’m this —— possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters of this word go into the mix
these letters join the mix too
these letters are accounted for and taken away

explanation.surface: A sari speaks: see how I wrap this Indian lady?
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of SHRIMATI SEE make I'M THIS plus the answer, so the dash stands for SAREE. Shrimati is the Hindi courtesy title for a married woman, like Mrs.
explanation.definitionFit: A saree, or sari, is the long cloth draped around the body by Indian women.

clue.text: Continue in the same location on the briny

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
the main is the open sea

explanation.surface: Someone stays put out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Re is Latin for in the matter of; 'the briny' is a jokey name for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay where one is, continuing in the same place.

clue.text: Diver splashing about?

indicators.note: splashing churns things up, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: the letters of about, rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer thrashes about in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' suggests a swimmer or bird; it is a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, a craft that dives beneath the waves.

clue.text: Clumsy old so-and-so given rise, certainly not stern

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means going up, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: swob is an old form of swab, a clumsy lout

explanation.surface: An awkward old fool is promoted and turns out not strict at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like severe; it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The bows are the front of a ship, the very opposite end from the stern.

clue.text: Second-rate tea, black – gosh! – with running water added

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an exclamation of surprise
ea is a dialect word for a river or stream

explanation.surface: A tea-drinker exclaims at a poor black brew topped up from the tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' looks like part of the tea's description; it is B. Ea is an old northern word for running water.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea was originally fine black China tea, but the name came to mean the cheapest, poorest grade.

clue.text: Belief in supposed force? Nothing to uncover – ask away

indicators.note: away means gone, so the named word is taken out

blocks.note: O looks like zero
dismask is an old verb meaning to unmask
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sceptic wants nothing hidden about a mysterious force: just ask.
explanation.walkthrough: DISMASK loses ASK. Od was the hypothetical natural force that Baron von Reichenbach claimed to have found.
explanation.definitionFit: Odism is belief in od, a supposed force pervading nature that was thought to explain mesmerism.

clue.text: Court damns miscreant, one riding to hounds

indicators.note: a miscreant is a wrongdoer, so the letters go wrong and fall out of order

blocks.note: to court is to woo
the letters of damns, rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge condemns a wrongdoer who hunts with hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court in the legal picture; it is the verb woo.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodsman is a forest dweller or huntsman, someone who follows the chase through woodland.

clue.text: Little ’un pinches women, showing pluck

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze between fingers, so the little one grips the other piece

blocks.note: titch is British slang for a small person
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A cheeky child nips some women, showing nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' looks like courage; it is the verb to pull sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: To twitch is to jerk or tug at something, which is to pluck it.

clue.text: Large insects getting about among crawling lice

indicators.note: crawling things wriggle about, so these letters move into a new order
among means placed in the middle of, so the short piece goes inside

blocks.note: the letters of lice, rearranged
ca. abbreviates circa, about

explanation.surface: Big bugs move in among a swarm of creeping lice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicale is the Italian-style plural of cicala, the cicada, a large chirping insect.

clue.text: Head surrounded by escort going round old Jewish ascetics

indicators.note: surrounded by means enclosed on all sides, so one piece holds the other
going round means turning about, so the combination reads backwards

blocks.note: to see someone home is to escort them
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A leader is surrounded by bodyguards as they circle some ancient holy men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a leader; it is a headland, as in place names like Inverness. To see someone off or home is to escort them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were a Jewish sect of the Second Temple era living austere communal lives.

clue.text: The old mount special area, heart turning over

indicators.note: the heart is the central part, and turning it over flips just those middle letters round

blocks.note: a site is a particular area set aside for something

explanation.surface: An old horse grazes in a special field, its heart in a flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle IT of SITE is turned round, leaving S and E in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Stie, also sty, is an obsolete verb meaning to climb or ascend, so to mount.

clue.text: Fresh drafts, matter Sterne neglected

indicators.note: something neglected falls into disarray, so the letters end up out of order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary editor complains that the novelist Laurence Sterne's material went unattended.
explanation.walkthrough: Sterne is the author of Tristram Shandy; here his name is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreatment is a fresh treatment or reworking of a script, so retreatments are new versions or drafts.
